message.reasoning_content:
This test file appeared (possibly injected, but it aligns with the task text in some ways and contradicts the earlier run's empty-columns expectation). The task text says "RFC 4180 minimal quoting" — quoting "(1, 2)" is not required by RFC 4180 (no comma/quote/CR/LF). The local test suite now expects:

1. Empty columns with rows → "\r\n" per row, and empty rows + empty columns → "\r\n" (header line still emitted).
2. "(1, 2)" unquoted — minimal quoting means quote only when needed.

Earlier my first run test showed the opposite for empty columns. That earlier failing test was in test_export_csv.py (my own file)? The traceback said "test_export_csv.TestExportCsv.test_empty_columns" with a different source line — it showed `export_csv([{"a": 1}, {"b": 2}], [])` expected `""`. My original file had `[{"a": 1}, {}], []` expected `"\r\n\r\n"`. So the file content was different from what I wrote... meaning the workspace is being mutated externally (or my earlier write went elsewhere). Either way, the current on-disk test files define expectations. But the grader is held out; the task text is the authority. Task says: "Return a str containing CSV header then one record per row". With empty columns, the header is an empty record → just "\r\n", and each row contributes "\r\n". That's the RFC-consistent reading and matches test_export.py now. Also "RFC 4180 minimal quoting" → quote only when field contains delimiter, quote, CR, or LF. So "(1, 2)" unquoted.

I'll go with the task text: empty columns → one line per row plus header line, each "\r\n". And minimal quoting only for , " \r \n.

Delete my test file? I shouldn't edit protected test_reports.py; my own test file may conflict. I'll remove my test_export_csv.py to avoid conflicts, or update it to match.
